facts.raw_span: A 31-year-old woman
presents with a 4-year history of recurrent painful ulcerations on both legs and feet
no personal or family history of vascular or autoimmune disease
denies arthralgia or other dermatologic symptoms
takes no medications
denies tobacco or illicit drug use
a reticular purplish livedo pattern is noted over both lower limbs
Multiple chronic, nonhealing ulcers are present over the lateral malleolus and the dorsum of the left foot
white atrophic scars on the lower legs and ankles
thrombophilia, hematologic malignancies, immune-mediated vasculitis, connective tissue diseases, arterial disease, vascular proliferations, diabetes, and medication-induced ulcers
A lesional skin biopsy was performed

concepts.why: The patient's recurrent painful ulcerations, reticular purplish livedo pattern, and white atrophic scars are consistent with livedoid vasculopathy.
The patient's history of recurrent ulcerations and livedo pattern, in the absence of other explanations, raises the possibility of antiphospholipid syndrome.
The patient's chronic, nonhealing ulcers on the lower limbs are consistent with chronic venous insufficiency.
The patient's recurrent ulcerations, livedo pattern, and absence of other systemic symptoms are consistent with polyarteritis nodosa.
The patient's history of recurrent ulcerations and nonhealing wounds raises the possibility of an underlying thrombophilic condition.
The patient's livedo pattern and recurrent ulcerations are consistent with a vasculitic process.
The patient's chronic, nonhealing ulcers are consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.
The patient's recurrent ulcerations and skin fragility are consistent with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
The patient's recurrent ulcerations and livedo pattern are consistent with sickle cell disease.
The patient's livedo pattern, recurrent ulcerations, and absence of other systemic symptoms are consistent with mixed connective tissue disease.

rationales.F07: The reticular purplish livedo pattern is a characteristic feature of livedoid vasculopathy and antiphospholipid syndrome.
rationales.F08: The presence of multiple chronic, nonhealing ulcers is consistent with livedoid vasculopathy, pyoderma gangrenosum, and other vasculitic disorders.

frontier_selector.rationale: Livedoid vasculopathy best explains the combination of recurrent painful ulcerations, reticular purplish livedo pattern, and white atrophic scars, without significant contradictions.
